chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: Ocean liner offer and the Elks convention band to Chicago
summary: Singer-drummer Freida Shaw offered Joe a ship job just as Mutt's band broke up to join an Elks marching band for Chicago, where Alex Hill and Pops Foster stayed.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: job came up on the ocean liner.
Oh, yeah, that's the next step. Tell me about that.

From the taxi dances, they had a woman named Freida Shaw that... For years she had singing choruses that sing in the movies for different background stuff and everything. And she was offered the job... And she played a little drums and she was a vocalist. So she offered the job to Big Boy and I, this tenor-man and myself. Because they wanted five pieces, I believe... Anyway, Big Boy didn't want to go. And at that very same time that all of this was happening, the Elks was organizing a band to go to Chicago at the Elks' Convention. So they were recruiting musicians. They wanted Mutt's whole band to go; I remember that. They had a detective named McDuff. I don't know if Bradley...Bradley was a foot patrolman or something at the time in Los Angeles or something... But Alton Redd, the drummer, knew Bradley real well in the later years; I know that, because they was friends. But anyway, Frank Passley(?)... That's when Mutt's band broke up. I want to put that in. Because Frank said, "Why don't you come on and go to Chicago with us." And I says, "Well, what are you going to play in a marching band?" He says, "I'm going to play some cymbals." And Alex Hill was going to play some
cymbals or snare drum or some kind of stuff. And Pops Foster played the tuba.
How big was this band that they were trying to get together?
They were trying to get a fairly big band, at least 15 to 18 pieces.
But it only lasted for the convention.

I think it stayed in Chicago about a week. You paid all your expenses... I forget what money it was. It wasn't too much money they offered you, but you got the trip and everything. So when they went back there, Alex Hill stayed.
He stayed in Chicago. He didn't come back. And Frank and I think Pops Foster did, too. George stayed back there; he didn't come back here.
